verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {applicant_name}, the Applicant herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above application are true and correct to my personal knowledge. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Applicant

promptInstructions: Draft an application for condonation of delay under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
S.5 applies to appeals and applications (not to suits — for suits, sec. 5 does not apply; specific extensions under sec. 12-14 may apply).
Cite Collector, Land Acquisition, Anantnag v. Mst. Katiji (1987) 2 SCC 107 — liberal approach to condone delay where 'sufficient cause' shown; substantial justice over technical considerations.
Cite Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy (2013) 12 SCC 649 — fifteen principles on condonation; rejection of mechanical approach.
Cite N. Balakrishnan v. M. Krishnamurthy (1998) 7 SCC 123 — length of delay is no matter; acceptability of explanation is sole criterion.
Cite Basawaraj v. Special Land Acquisition Officer (2013) 14 SCC 81 — sufficient cause must be such as to prevent applicant from filing within time despite due diligence.
Para 1: Description of impugned order — court, date, decree/order/judgment.
Para 2: Period of limitation prescribed — cite Article of Limitation Act Schedule. Common: appeal under CPC Art. 116 (30/90 days); revision Art. 124 (90 days); review O.47 (30 days); etc.
Para 3: Date when certified copy applied for and received — to claim deduction under S.12(2).
Para 4: Last date of limitation and actual / proposed date of filing — quantify delay in days.
Para 5: Sufficient cause — must explain every day of delay where delay exceeds 30 days; for very short delays, broad explanation may suffice but day-by-day is safer.

Common grounds: medical illness (with certificate), bereavement (with death certificate), pursuit of wrong remedy in good faith, advocate's negligence (Rafiq v. Munshilal AIR 1981 SC 1400 — litigant should not suffer for counsel's lapse), administrative delays in obtaining certified copies, pendency of related proceedings.
Para 6: Specific events — date-wise narrative — what applicant did each day to pursue remedy.
Para 7: Bona fides — no negligence, no mala fide, no want of due diligence.
Where applicant is government / public body: Cite State of Nagaland v. Lipok AO (2005) 3 SCC 752 — slightly liberal but not blanket; impersonal machinery considerations.

Where delay is inordinate (years): Cite Pundlik Jalam Patil v. Executive Engineer (2008) 17 SCC 448; Postmaster General v. Living Media India (2012) 3 SCC 563 — government cannot get away with stock excuses.
Where the matter involves valuable rights or property: courts more inclined to condone if explanation reasonable.
DO NOT mechanically cite Mst. Katiji — must build factual sufficient cause first.
Note S.5 NOT applicable to suits; for suits, see S.3 (bar) and S.12-14 (exclusion/extension).
Where time-barred SARFAESI, NI Act, NCDRC matters — many have own limitation regimes (e.g., NI Act S.142(b) proviso 30-day condonation power); cite specific statute.
Affidavit in support is mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Bar of limitation — dismissal of time-barred proceedings even if not raised
Expiry of period when court is closed
Extension of prescribed period — sufficient cause for appeals and applications
Exclusion of time in legal proceedings
Exclusion of time for obtaining certified copy
Exclusion of time of bona fide proceeding in wrong court

filing_checklist: Certified copy application receipt and delivery date proof
Medical certificates / death certificates / travel records (if applicable)
Advocate's correspondence / certificate (if attributing delay to counsel)
Court fee per state Schedule (usually fixed for IA)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: impugned_order_date must be valid date in past
If delay_in_days > 30, day_by_day_explanation must not be empty
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
TIME-BAR CHECK: confirm impugned_order_date with relevant Article of Limitation Act
